x: We have already explained the meaning of His saying, “Ha Meem. The revelation of the Book,” so there is no need to repeat it in this topic.
His saying:
h
The revelation of the Book is from God
, the Almighty, the Wise.
And His statement,
h
And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except in truth

, God Almighty says: We did not create the heavens and the earth and bring them into being as a manufactured creation, and what is between them of the kinds of world except in truth, meaning: except to establish truth and justice in creation. And His saying, And a specified term, means: Except for a term for all of that that is known to Him, and He will destroy it when it reaches it, and will annihilate it after it had existed by His bringing it into existence. And His statement,
h
And those who disbelieve turn away from that which they have been warned of
. God Almighty says: And those who have denied the Oneness of God turn away from God’s warning to them and do not reflect and take heed.

God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists among your al-Nas 114:Have you seen, O people, the gods and idols that you worship besides God? Show me what they created from the earth. My Lord created the entire earth, and you called it because of its creation. I did not create any gods or lords from that. So that will be an argument for you in your worship of it. For part of My argument for My worship of My God and My singling out Him as God is that He created the earth and innovated it from nothing. And His statement,
h
Or do they have a partner in the heavens

? God Almighty says: Or do your gods that you worship, O people, have a partner with God in the seven heavens, so that you will have an argument for your worship of them? For part of my argument for my singling out worship for my Lord is that He has no partner in creating them, and that He is the One who created them, without everything else besides Him.
And His saying,
h
Bring me a book from before this

, God Almighty says: A book that came from God before this Qur’an that was sent down to me, that the gods and idols that you worship created something from the earth, or that they have a partner with God in the heavens, so that will be an argument for you for your worship of them, because if that is true for them, then their partnership in the blessings that you have is true, and it is obligatory for them to thank you, and they deserve service from you because that is something that no one can create except God. And his saying, or a trace of knowledge, the reciters differed in their recitation of that, so the majority of the reciters of Hijaz and Iraq read it as or a trace of knowledge with an alif, meaning: bring me a remnant of knowledge. Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami said that he used to read it as or a trace of knowledge meaning: or specifically from the knowledge that you were given, and you preferred it over others.

The other recitation that I do not permit is or a trace of knowledge with an alif, due to the consensus of the reciters of the regions on it. The commentators differed in their interpretation of this verse.

Some of them said: Its meaning is: Or bring me knowledge that your gods created something from the earth and that they have a share in the heavens through the line that you draw on the earth, for you Arabs are people of divination, augury, and soothsaying.
Who said that?

c: Bishr bin Adam told us: Abu Al-Asim told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Safwan bin Salim, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Or a trace of knowledge. He said: A line that the Arabs used to draw on the ground.

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Abu Bakr said:
m: meaning Ibn Ayyash: The line is divination.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: or specifically from knowledge.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada:
m: Or a trace of knowledge. He said: Or a special kind of knowledge.
b.via: Muammar on the authority of Qatada

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: Or a trace of knowledge. He said: That is, a special kind of knowledge.

c: Abdul Warith bin Abdul Samad bin Abdul Warith told us: My father told me, on the authority of Al-Hussein, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Or a trace of knowledge. He said: Especially knowledge.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Or knowledge that you stir up and extract.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement, or a trace of knowledge, he said: A trace of something they extract by nature.
b.via: Muammar on the authority of al-Hasan

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Or do you influence that knowledge from someone before you?
Who said that?

m: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said:

x: God Almighty says: And which servant is more astray than a servant who calls upon gods other than God who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection? He says: His call will never be answered because it is a stone or wood or something similar. And His statement, And they are heedless of their invocation, meaning that the Most High says: And their gods whom they call upon are heedless of their invocations, because they do not hear, speak, or understand. What He meant by describing them as heedless is that He likens them to a person who is forgetful of what is said to him, since they do not understand anything that is said to them, just as something is said to them, just as someone who is heedless of something does not understand what he is heedless of. This is a rebuke from God to these polytheists for their bad opinion and the ugliness of their choice in their worship of someone who does not reason or understand, and for abandoning the worship of all of His blessings that they have, and the one to whom they seek help when needs and calamities befall them.

It was said: the one who does not respond to Him, so mentioning the gods, which are inanimate, is embarrassing, while mentioning the sons of Adam and the one who has choice and discrimination, is embarrassing, since their worshippers had likened them to kings and princes who serve them in their service. Thus, the discussion of that was conducted in a manner that was common among them.

God Almighty says: And when the people are gathered on the Day of Resurrection for the Day of Judgment, these gods that they called upon in this world will be their enemies because they will disown them. And they were disbelievers in their worship. God Almighty says: And their gods that they worshipped in this world will be disbelievers in their worship because they will say on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:We did not command them to worship us, nor did we feel that they worshipped us. We disown them, O our Lord.
And His statement,
h
And when Our clear verses are recited to them

, God Almighty says: And when Our verses are recited to these polytheists among your people, meaning Our arguments that We used against them, in what We sent down of Our Book to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, clear meaning clear and luminous. Those who disbelieved said of the truth when it came to them, God Almighty says: Those who strove to believe in the oneness of God and denied His Messenger said of the truth when it came to them from God, so He sent it down to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, This is obvious magic, meaning this Qur'an is a deception that deceives us and takes hold of the hearts of those who hear it, the work of magic. Clear, He says: It makes clear to those who contemplate it from those who hear it that it is obvious magic.

God Almighty says: Or do these polytheists from Quraysh say: Muhammad invented this Qur’an, fabricated it and fabricated it as a lie? Say to them, O Muhammad, if you fabricated it and fabricated it as a lie about God, then you have no power over me meaning you will not be able to protect me from God if He punishes me for inventing it and fabricating anything about it, and you will not be able to ward off any harm from me if He afflicts me with it. And His statement, He knows best what you say about it, means: My Lord knows best what you say among yourselves regarding this Qur’an. The ha in His statement, you say about it, is from the mention of the Qur’an. And in a similar manner to what we said about the meaning of His statement, You will overflow therein, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement when you are pouring forth therein, he said: You say. And His saying,
h
That is sufficient as a witness between me and you

, means: God is sufficient as a witness against me and against you regarding what you say of your denial of me in what I brought to you from God, the Forgiving, the Most Merciful, that He will not punish them for it after they repent from it.

x: God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of your people from Quraysh,
h
I am not an innovation among the messengers

. Meaning: I am not the first of the messengers that God sent to His creation. There were many messengers before me who were sent to nations before you. It is said: He is an innovation in this, and an innovation in it, if he was the first in it. Among the innovations is the saying of Adi bin Zaid. I am not an exception to the incidents that befall men who have become naked after their misery and happiness. It is a beautiful saying of Al-Ahwas: I was proud and said, “Look at me. It is not out of ignorance that I have brought something new.” It means first, it is said: He is an innovation from an innovation-oriented people. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Muawiyah told me, Ali told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
I am not an innovation among the messengers
, meaning: I am not the first of the messengers.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me, my uncle told me, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
I am not an innovation among the messengers
, he said: He says: I was not the first messenger sent.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
I was not an innovation among the messengers
, he said: I was not the first of them.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muawiyah told us on the authority of Abu Hubayrah, who said:
m: I asked Qatada, Say, ‘
h
I am not an innovation among the messengers
.’ He said: That is, there were messengers before me.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, Say, ‘
h
I am not an innovation among the messengers
,’ meaning: that there were messengers before me.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, an innovation among the messengers, he said, There were messengers before him. And His saying,
h
And I do not know what will be done with me or with you
, the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation.

x: Some of them said: It refers to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it was said to him: Say to the believers in you, I do not know what will be done with me or with you on the Day of Resurrection, and to what we will be destined there. They said: Then God explained to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to the believers in him their state in the Hereafter, and it was said to him, Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, * That God may forgive you what preceded of your sin and what will come after Al-Fath 48:1-2. And He said, That He may admit the believing men and believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow, to abide therein eternally, and He may remove from them their misdeeds Al-Fath 48:5.
Who said that?

c: Ali told us: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
And I do not know what will be done with me or with you

. Then God revealed after this: So that God may forgive you your sins, past and future. Ibn Hamid narrated: Yahya bin Wadh narrated from Al-Hussein from Yazid from Ikrimah and Al-Hussein Al-Basri, they said: Ha Mim Al-Ahqaf said: “
h
And I do not know what will be done with me or with you

. I only follow what is revealed to me, and I am not but a clear warner.” Then it was abrogated by the verse in Surat al-Fath 48:Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, so that God may forgive you. Al-Fath 1-2… the verse. So the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out when this verse was revealed, and he gave them the good report that he had been forgiven for his past and future sins. He said to him: “There are men from among the believers.

x: God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who say about this Qur’an when it came to them, This is obvious magic. “Have you considered, O people, if this Qur’an is from God, He sent it down to me, and you disbelieved in it?” He says: And you denied it. And his statement,
h
And a witness from among the Children of Israel bore witness to the like of it
, the people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of that.
Some of them said: Its meaning is:
h
And a witness from among the Children of Israel bore witness to the like of it
, meaning the like of the Qur’an. They said: And the like of the Qur’an to which Moses bore witness to the truthfulness of the Torah.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-Wahhab told us: Dawud told us, on the authority of Aamer, on the authority of Masruq,
m: regarding this verse:
h
And a witness from among the Children of Israel testified to something similar

to it. So the disbelievers among the people of Mecca disputed over it. The Torah is like the Qur’an, and Moses is like Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated: Abd al-A’la narrated: Dawud was asked about the verse, Say, ‘Have you considered, if it is from God and you disbelieve in it?’… The verse. Dawud said, ‘Amir said, Masruq said: By God, it was not revealed about Abdullah ibn Salam. It was only revealed in Mecca, and Abdullah did not convert to Islam except in Medina. But it was a dispute that Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, argued with his people about. He said: So the verse, Say, ‘Have you considered, if it is from God and you disbelieve in it and a witness from among the Children of Israel testifies to the like of it and believes while you are arrogant’ was revealed. He said: So the Torah is like the Qur’an and Moses is like Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. So they believed in the Torah and their Messenger, and you disbelieved. Abu Kurayb narrated: Ibn Idris narrated: I heard Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said: Some people claim that a witness from among the Children of Israel testified to something similar to it, namely Abdullah ibn Salam. Abdullah only converted to Islam in Medina, and Masruq informed me that Surah Ha Mim was only revealed in Mecca, and that it was the argument of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with his people, and he said: Have you considered if it is from God meaning the Qur’an and you disbelieved in it,
h
and a witness from among the Children of Israel testified to something similar
to it and believed Moses and Muhammad, may God bless them both, are upon the Criterion.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said:
m: Some people claim that the witness to something like it is Abdullah ibn Salam, but Abdullah only converted to Islam in Medina.

c: Masruq informed me that
m: Al-Ha Meem was only revealed in Mecca, and it was the Messenger of God’s argument with his people, so he said: Say, ‘Have you considered if it is from God’ meaning the Criterion and a witness from among the Children of Israel testifies to something like it, so the Torah is like the Criterion. Moses testified to the Torah, and Muhammad testified to the Criterion, may God bless them both and grant them peace.

c: Yaqub told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Dawud told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq,
m: Say, "Have you considered: if it is from God, and you disbelieve in it, and a witness from among the Children of Israel bears witness to something similar to it and believes, while you are arrogant? Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people." regarding His statement, Say, ‘Have you considered, if it is from God?’… the verse, he said: Ibn Salam’s conversion to Islam occurred in Medina, and this surah was revealed in Mecca. It was only a dispute between Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his people, so He said, Say, ‘Have you considered, if it is from God, and you disbelieve in it, and a witness from among the Children of Israel testifies to something similar to it?’ He said: The Torah is like the Criterion, and Moses is like Muhammad, so he believed in him, and you were arrogant. Then He said: This one from among Israel believed in his prophet and his book, and you were arrogant, so you denied your prophet and your book. Indeed, God does not guide.… until His statement, This is an ancient falsehood.

x: Others said: What is meant by his statement,
h
And a witness from among the Children of Israel bore witness to the like of it

, is Abdullah ibn Salam. They said: The meaning of the statement is, And a witness from among the Children of Israel bore witness to the like of this Qur’an, confirming it. They said: And the like of the Qur’an is the Torah.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Abdullah bin Yusuf al-Tanisi told us, he said:
m: I heard Malik bin Anas narrating on the authority of Abu al-Nadr, on the authority of Amir bin Saad bin Abi Waqqas, on the authority of his father, he said: “I never heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say about anyone walking on the earth that he is from the people of Paradise except for Abdullah bin Salam. He said: And in him was revealed: ‘
h
And a witness from among the Children of Israel bore witness to the like of it

c: Al-Husayn bin Ali Al-Sada’i told us: Abu Dawud Al-Tayalisi told us: Shu’ayb bin Safwan told us: Abdul Malik bin Umair told us that
m: Muhammad bin Yusuf bin Abdullah bin Salam said: Abdullah said: It was revealed regarding Say, ‘Have you considered, if it is from God’… until His saying then you believed and were arrogant.

c: Ali bin Saeed bin Masruq Al-Kindi told me: Abu Muhammad bin Ya’la told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Umair, on the authority of my nephew Abdullah bin Salamah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Salam:
m: It was revealed regarding “
h
And a witness from among the Children of Israel bore witness to the like of it
, so he believed, and you were arrogant. Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people.”

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: regarding his statement, Say, ‘Have you considered, if it is from God’… the verse, he said: “There was a man from the People of the Book who believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said, ‘Would you accept that ʿAbdullah ibn Salam judge between me and you? Do you believe?’ They said, ‘Yes.’ So he sent for ʿAbdullah ibn Salam and said, ‘Do you bear witness that I am the Messenger of God, written in the Torah and the Gospel?’ He said, ‘Yes.’ So the Jews refused, and ʿAbdullah ibn Salam became a Muslim.”
b.via: his father on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hussein told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the words of God Almighty: And a witness from among the Children of Israel testified to the like of it, he said: Abdullah bin Salam.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: “Say: Have you considered if it is from God...” The verse. We were told that Abdullah bin Salam believed in the Book of God, in His Messenger, and in Islam, and he was one of the Jewish rabbis.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada
m: regarding his statement,
h
And a witness from among the Children of Israel testified to something similar
. He said: He is Abdullah ibn Salam.
b.via: Muammar on the authority of Qatada

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Mu’adh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
And a witness from among the Children of Israel testified to something similar

, the witness was Abdullah ibn Salam, who was one of the rabbis and scholars of the Children of Israel. “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent to the Jews, and they came to him. He asked them, saying: ‘Do you know that I am the Messenger of God and you find me written down with you in the Torah?’ They said: ‘We do not know what you say, and we disbelieve in what you have brought.’ He said: ‘Which man is Abdullah ibn Salam among you?’ They said: ‘Our scholar and the best of us.’ He said: ‘Would you be satisfied with him between me and you?’ They said: ‘Yes.’ So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent for Abdullah ibn Salam, and he came to him and said: ‘What is your testimony, O Ibn Salam?’ He said: ‘I bear witness that you are the Messenger of God and that your book came from God.’ So he believed and they disbelieved. God, the Blessed and Exalted, says: ‘So he believed and you were arrogant.’”

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Aouf narrated to us, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: saying: It reached me that when ʿAbdullah ibn Salam wanted to convert to Islam, he said: Aouf narrated to us, on the authority of al-Hasan, saying: It reached me that when ʿAbdullah ibn Salam wanted to convert to Islam, he said: O Messenger of God, the Jews know that I am one of their scholars, and that my father was one of their scholars, and I bear witness that you are the Messenger of God and that they find you written with them in the Torah, so send to so-and-so and so-and-so, and whoever he named from the Jews, and

x: God the Most High says: “And those who denied the prophethood of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) from among the Jews of the Children of Israel said to those who believed in him, ‘If your belief in Muhammad and what he brought you had been any good, you would not have preceded us in believing in him.’” This interpretation is according to the view of those who interpreted His statement,
h
And a witness from among the Children of Israel testified to the like of it

, as meaning that it refers to Abdullah ibn Salam. However, according to the interpretation of those who interpreted it as referring to the polytheists of Quraysh, then the interpretation of His statement,
h
And those who disbelieved said to those who believed

, ‘If it had been any good, they would not have preceded us to it,’ should be directed to referring to the polytheists of Quraysh. This is how Qatada interpreted it, and in his interpretation of it, he also left out his interpretation of His statement,
h
And a witness from among the Children of Israel testified to the like of it
, as meaning that it refers to Abdullah ibn Salam.
He mentioned the narration about him:

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And those who disbelieved said to those who believed

, ‘If it had been good, they would not have preceded us to it.’ He said: Those were some of the polytheists who said that: We are more honorable, we, we. If it had been good, so-and-so and so-and-so would not have preceded us to it. Indeed, God chooses for His mercy whomever He wills.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And those who disbelieved said to those who believed

, ‘If it had been good, they would not have preceded us to it.’ He said: This was said by some people who were more powerful than them in the Age of Ignorance. They said, By God, if this had been good, the sons of so-and-so would not have preceded us to it. God chooses for His mercy whomever He wills and honors whomever He wills. Blessed and Exalted be He. And His statement,
h
And when they were not guided by it

, God Almighty says: And when they did not see Muhammad and what he brought from God of guidance, so that they would be guided by it to the straight path, they will say, ‘This is an ancient falsehood,’ meaning: They will say, “This Qur’an that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought is from the ancient report of the ancients,” as God Almighty said, informing about them: And they say, ‘Legends of the ancients which he wrote down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening.’ (al-Furqan 25:5)

x: The Most High says: And before this Book, there was the Book of Moses, which is the Torah, a guide for the Children of Israel to follow and a mercy for them which We sent down to them. The speech was presented as a report about the Book without mentioning the full report, as the speech is sufficient to indicate its completion, and its completion is: And before it was a Book of Moses, which is the Torah, a guide and a mercy which We sent down in the Arabic language. The Arabs differed in their interpretation of this and in the nominative meaning of an Arabic tongue.
Some of the grammarians of Basra said: the tongue and the Arab are in the accusative case.

Some of them said that on the authority of made the book like the truth of the tongue. According to the one who made the tongue in the accusative case as a state, and made the book one of its attributes, the interpretation of the statement should be: And this book is in the Arabic tongue confirming the Torah, the book of Moses, that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and that what he brought from God is the truth. As for the second statement that we have narrated from some of them, that he made the nominative case of the tongue confirming, this statement has no meaning because that would then be interpreted thus, except that the one who confirms himself, because the Arabic tongue is this book, unless he makes the Arabic tongue Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and directs his interpretation to: And this book, which is the Qur’an, confirms Muhammad, which is the Arabic tongue. Then that would be one face of interpretation.

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: His saying an Arabic tongue is an adjective for the book, and it is in the accusative case because it is in it: And this is a book that confirms the Torah and the Gospel in the Arabic tongue, so an Arabic tongue is derived from yesdiq because it is a verb, just as you say: I passed by a man standing, doing good, and I passed by a man standing doing good. He said: If the Arabic tongue had been raised, it would have been permissible as an adjective for the book. It has been mentioned that this is in the reading of Ibn Masoud: And this is a Book confirming what was before it in an Arabic tongue. So according to this reading, the accusative case in his saying in an Arabic tongue is directed from two aspects: One of them is based on what I have explained, that the tongue is outside of his saying confirming, and the other: that it is a cut from the ha’ in between you.

The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that it is in the accusative case as a state of what is in confirming of the mention of the book, because his saying confirming is a verb, so the interpretation of the statement, if that is the case, is: This Qur’an confirms the book of Moses that Muhammad is a prophet sent in the Arabic language. And His saying,
h
To warn those who have wronged
, means: To warn this book that We sent down to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, those who have wronged themselves by disbelieving in God and worshipping other than Him. His statement,
h
And good tidings to the doers of good

, means: It is good tidings for those who obeyed God and did good in their faith and obedience to Him in this world, so good is the reward from God in the hereafter for their obedience to Him. In His statement,
h
And good tidings
, there are two ways of parsing: The nominative case is in apposition to the Book, meaning: And this is a confirming Book
h
and good tidings to the doers of good
The accusative case is in apposition to the Book, meaning: And this is a confirming Book
h
and good tidings to the doers of good

. So if He replaces gives good tidings with good tidings or glad tidings, it is in the accusative case, just as you would say, I came to you to visit you and to honor you and to fulfill your right, meaning to visit you and honor you and fulfill your right. So honor and fulfillment are in the accusative case with an implied meaning. The reciters differed in their reading of linadhir. The majority of the reciters of Hijaz read it with a ta', meaning: Let you warn, O Muhammad. The majority of the reciters of Iraq read it with a ya', meaning: Let the Book warn. Whichever of the two readings that reciter reads, he is correct.

evidence.text: It has been mentioned that this is in the reading of Ibn Masoud: And this is a Book confirming what was before it in an Arabic tongue.

So according to this reading, the accusative case in his saying in an Arabic tongue is directed from two aspects: One of them is based on what I have explained, that the tongue is outside of his saying confirming, and the other: that it is a cut from the ha’ in between you.
The reciters differed in their reading of linadhir.
The majority of the reciters of Hijaz read it with a ta', meaning: Let you warn, O Muhammad.
The majority of the reciters of Iraq read it with a ya', meaning: Let the Book warn.
Whichever of the two readings that reciter reads, he is correct.

x: God Almighty says: Indeed, those who say, ‘Our Lord is God,’ other than whom there is no god, and then remain steadfast in their belief in that, not mixing it with polytheism and not disobeying God in His commands and prohibitions, there will be no fear concerning them from the terrors and horrors of the Day of Resurrection, nor will they grieve over what they left behind after their death.
And His statement,
h
Those are the companions of Paradise

, God Almighty says: Those who said this statement and were righteous are the people of Paradise and its inhabitants. They will abide therein, meaning: they will remain there forever. As a reward for what they used to do, meaning: as a reward from Us to them, which We gave them for the righteous deeds they used to do in this world.

God Almighty says: And We have enjoined upon the son of Adam, concerning his parents, good treatment of them during their lifetime, and righteousness towards them during their lifetime and after their death. The reciters differed in their reading of His statement hasan. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read it as hasan with a damma on the ha', according to the interpretation I have described. The most knowledgeable reciters of Kufa read it as ihsanan with an alif, meaning: And we enjoined upon him to be good to them. Whichever of them he recites is correct, due to the similarity of the meanings and the prevalence of each reading among the reciters. And His statement,
h
His mother carried him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship
, means that God Almighty says: And We have enjoined upon man, to his parents, good treatment and dutifulness to them, because he was from them to him as a pregnancy, a birth, and a growth.

Then God, the Most High, described the blessing of his mother, and what she experienced from him during the state of carrying him and giving birth to him, and alerted him to the duty he owes to her of dutifulness, and her deserving of his honor and good companionship. So He said, His mother carried him, meaning in her womb with hardship, meaning with difficulty, and gave birth to him with hardship, meaning: and gave birth to him with hardship, meaning with difficulty.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: His mother carried him with difficulty and gave birth to him with difficulty. He said: She carried him with difficulty and gave birth to him with difficulty.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada and al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement,
h
His mother carried him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship
, they said: She carried him with difficulty and gave birth to him with difficulty.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, that Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement,
h
His mother carried him unwillingly

, he said: It was difficult for her. The reciters differed in their recitation of the phrase unwillingly. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read it unwillingly with a fat-ha on the kaf, and the majority of the reciters of Kufa read it unwillingly with a damma on it. I have explained the difference of opinion among those who differed in this regard before, If it is fat-ha or if it is damma in Surat Al-Baqarah, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings, with similar meanings, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct. And His statement,
h
And his carrying and weaning is thirty months
, God Almighty says: And his mother

x: God Almighty says: Those who have this characteristic are the ones from whom the best of what they did in this world of righteous deeds will be accepted, and He will reward them for it and recompense them for it. And We overlook their misdeeds meaning: And He will pardon them for the misdeeds that they did in this world, and He will not punish them for them. For the companions of Paradise meaning: We will do that to them, as we did for the companions of Paradise and its people who are its people.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Hakam ibn Abaan, on the authority of Al-Ghatrif, on the authority of Jabir ibn Zayd, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: on the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the authority of the Trustworthy Spirit, who said: “The good deeds and bad deeds of the servant will be brought and will be recompensed for one another. If one good deed remains, God will expand Paradise for him.” He said: “So I entered upon him and he increased it, and he narrated something similar to this hadith. I said: ‘What if the good deed is lost?’ He said: ‘Those are the ones from whom We accept the best of what they did and overlook their misdeeds. ’... the verse.” Ibn Humayd narrated: Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Abu Bakr called Umar, may God be pleased with them both, and said to him: I have given you a recommendation that you should memorize: God has a right at night that He does not accept during the day, a right that He does not accept during the night. No one has a voluntary prayer until he performs the obligatory prayer. The scales of those whose scales are heavy on the Day of Resurrection will be heavy because they followed the truth in this world, and that was heavy for them. It is right for a scale in which nothing but the truth is placed to be heavy, and the scales of those whose scales are light on the Day of Resurrection will be light because they followed falsehood in this world and that was light for them. It is right for a scale in which nothing but falsehood is placed to be light. Have you not seen that God mentioned the people of Paradise with their best deeds, and someone says: How do my deeds compare to the deeds of these people? That is because God Almighty overlooks their worst deeds and does not reveal them. Have you not seen that God mentioned the people of Hell with their worst deeds, so someone says: I am better in deeds than these people. That is because God returned to them their best deeds. Have you not seen that God has in His hand the power to destroy, and He wishes from God a wish that is not true. The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement,
h
We accept from them the best of what they did and overlook

. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra and some of the reciters of Kufa read it as yattaqubal and wa-tajidhu with a damma on the ya’ between them, and on what the agent is not named, and they raised ahsan. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as nataqubal and wa-natajidhu with a noon and a fatha on it, and they lowered ahsan with the meaning of God Almighty informing them about Himself that He will do that to them, and in response to the statement of His statement,
h
And We have enjoined upon man and We accept from them the best of what they did and overlook
. They are two well-known readings with correct meaning, so whichever one the reciter recites, he is correct. And His statement,
h
The promise of truth which they were promised
, means: God promised them this promise,
h
the promise of truth
, there is no doubt that He will fulfill it for them, which they were promised in this world after them, God Almighty. And His statement,
h
The promise of truth

, is in the accusative case because the source is outside of His statement, He accepts from them the best of what they did and overlooks their bad deeds. And He only excluded from this statement the source of He promised a promise, because His statement,
h
He accepts from them and overlooks is a promise from God to them
, so He said,
h
The promise of truth
, according to that meaning.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement, We accept from them the best of what they did and overlook.

The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra and some of the reciters of Kufa read it as yattaqubal and wa-tajidhu with a damma on the ya’ between them, and on what the agent is not named, and they raised ahsan.

The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as nataqubal and wa-natajidhu with a noon and a fatha on it, and they lowered ahsan with the meaning of God Almighty informing them about Himself that He will do that to them, and in response to the statement of His statement, And We have enjoined upon man and We accept from them the best of what they did and overlook.

x: And this is a description from God, the Most High, with which we describe a misguided disbeliever, and a disobedient one towards his parents, while they are striving to advise him and call him to God. Their calling him to the truth and their advice to him only increases his insolence and rebellion against God, and his persistence in his ignorance. God, the Most High, says:
h
And he who said to his parents

, that they called him to belief in God, and the acknowledgment of God’s resurrection of His creation from their graves, and His recompense to them for their deeds, Fie upon you both, meaning: filth and stench upon you.
h
Do you promise me that I will come forth
? meaning:
h
Do you promise me that I will come forth
from my grave after my annihilation and trial, alive?

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: Do you promise me that I will come out? That I will be resurrected after death.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada
m: regarding his statement,
h
Do you promise me that I will come forth
? He said: He means the resurrection after death.
b.via: Muammar on the authority of Qatada

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me:
m: On the authority of his father: On the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement,
h
And he who said to his parents
, ‘Fie upon you!
h
Do you promise me that I will come forth
?’… to the end of the verse. He said: The one who said this was a son of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him. He said,
h
Do you promise me that I will come forth
?: Do you promise me that I will be resurrected after death?

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Hudha told us: Aouf told us on the authority of Al-Hasan
m: regarding his statement,
h
And he who said to his parents
, ‘Fie upon you! Do you promise me that I will be brought forth?’ He said: He is the disbelieving, immoral person who is disobedient to his children and denies the resurrection.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us, Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: Then he described a bad servant who was disobedient to his parents and wicked, saying:
h
And he who said to his parents
, ‘Fie upon you both’... until His saying: Legends of the ancients. And His statement:
h
And generations have passed before me

means: Do you promise me that I will be resurrected, while generations have passed before me, and they perished and none of them were resurrected? And if I were to be resurrected after my death, as you say, then those generations who perished before me would have been resurrected. And they are calling upon God means, the Most High said, and his parents are calling upon God to help him, and they are calling upon Him to believe in God and acknowledge the resurrection, and they are saying to him, Woe to you! Believe, meaning, believe in God’s promise and acknowledge that you will be resurrected after your death. Indeed, the promise of God, which He promised His creation, that He will raise them from their graves and bring them forth from them to the place of reckoning to be rewarded for their deeds, is true, without doubt. So the enemy of God says, responding to his parents and rejecting their advice, and denying God’s promise: What is this that you are saying to me and calling me to, that I will be resurrected after my death from my grave, except what the people of old wrote of falsehoods, so they wrote it, and you two were right and spoke the truth.
h
And he who said to his parents

, "Fie upon you! Do you promise me that I will be brought forth, while generations before me have passed away?" And they both cry out to God for help. "Woe to you! Believe! Indeed, the promise of God is truth!" And he will say, "This is not but legends of the former peoples."

x: God Almighty says: These are the ones who have this description, upon whom God’s punishment is due, and upon whom His chastisement and wrath have befallen, among those upon whom God’s punishment has befallen in the same way as it befell these nations of the jinn and mankind who have passed away, who denied God’s messengers and rebelled against the command of their Lord. And His statement, Indeed, they were losers, means that God Almighty says: They were the ones who were deceived by selling guidance for misguidance and comfort for punishment.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Muadh bin Hisham told us: My father told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said:
m: The jinn do not die. Qatada said: So I said: Those are the ones upon whom the word has come into effect among nations that have passed on.

x: And His statement,
h
And for all are degrees according to what they have done

, the Most High says: For all of these two groups: the group of belief in God and the Last Day and being dutiful to parents, and the group of disbelief in God and the Last Day and being disobedient to parents, whose characteristics our Lord, the Most High, has described in these verses, are stations and ranks with God on the Day of Resurrection, according to what they have done, meaning from the deeds that they do in this world, whether good or bad, God will reward them for them.

c: Yunus told me that Ibn Wahb told us that Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
And for all are degrees according to what they have done

, that the degrees of the people of Hell will go downward, and the degrees of the people of Paradise will go upward. And that He may fully recompense them for their deeds, that is, the Most High says, “And that He may give all of them the rewards for the deeds that they did in this world. The good-doer among them will receive, through his goodness, what God has promised of honor, and the evil-doer among them will receive only punishment for his sin, not for what he did not do, nor will he be held responsible for the sin of another. The good-doer among them will not be deprived of the reward for his goodness.

x: God Almighty says, And on the Day those who disbelieved will be exposed to the Fire, it will be said to them, ‘You consumed your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them.’

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And the Day those who disbelieved are exposed to the Fire

, Yazid recited until he reached, and for what you used to commit, you know, by God, that some people keep their good deeds. A man kept his good deeds back if he was able, and there is no power except with God. It was mentioned that Umar ibn al-Khattab used to say, If I wished, I would have the best food among you and the softest clothing among you, but I keep my good deeds back. It was mentioned to us that when he came to Syria, food was prepared for him, the likes of which had never been seen before. He said, This is for us, but what about the poor Muslims who died without being satisfied with barley bread? Khalid ibn al-Walid said, Paradise is for them. Umar’s eyes welled up, and he said, If our share is in the ruins, and they have gone - Abu Jaʿfar said, As far as I can see - with Paradise, then they have been far removed from us.” “It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered upon the people of the Suffa, a place where the poor Muslims gathered, and they were patching their clothes with leather as they could not find any patches for them. He said: ‘Are you better today, or is it a day when one of you goes out in the morning in one garment and returns in another, and is fed with a bowl and taken away with another, and his house is covered as the Kaaba is covered?’ They said: ‘We will be better on that day.’ He said: ‘Rather, you are better today.’”

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, who said: Saheb told us on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said:
m: “Our food with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was only two black things: water and dates. By God, we did not see this brown one of yours, nor did we know what it was.” He said: Saeed narrated to us on the authority of Qatada on the authority of Abu Burda bin Abdullah bin Qais Al-Ash’ari on the authority of his father: “O my son, if you had witnessed us with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we were with our Prophet when the rain fell upon us, you would have thought that our scent was the scent of sheep, for our clothing was wool.”

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about the statement of God Almighty: You have spent your good things in your worldly life… to the end of the verse. Then he recited: Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment - We fully repay them for their deeds therein, and they will not be deprived. And he recited: “Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter - We increase for him his harvest. And whoever desires the harvest of this world - We give him thereof.” And he recited: Whoever desires the immediate - We hasten for him therein what We will for whom We intend.… to the end of the verse. And he said: These are the ones who spent their good things in their worldly life. The reciters differed in their recitation of the statement, You have gone away, your good things. The majority of reciters in the regions recited it as you have gone away without a question, except for Abu Jaʿfar al-Qariʿ, who recited it as a question. The Arabs ask questions with rebuke and leave out the question in it, so they say, Did you go away and do such and such? or Did you go away, so you did, and Did you do? The more impressive of the two recitations is the omission of the question in it, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it, and because it is the more eloquent of the two languages. And His statement,
h
So today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation

, God Almighty says: It will be said to them: So today, O disbelievers who consumed your good things in their worldly life, you will be recompensed, meaning you will be rewarded with the punishment of humiliation, meaning the punishment of disgrace, and that is the punishment of the Fire that humiliates them.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told us: Abu Asim told us:
m: Isa told
