The majority of reciters in the regions recited it as you have gone away without a question, except for Abu Jaʿfar al-Qariʿ, who recited it as a question.
The more impressive of the two recitations is the omission of the question in it, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it, and because it is the more eloquent of the two languages.

x: God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: And mention, O Muhammad, to your people who reject you, what you have brought them of the truth, Hud, the brother of Aad. Indeed, God has sent you to them as He had sent him to Aad. So, fear that the punishment of God will befall them for their disbelief, as befell them when they denied Our Messenger Hud to them, when he warned his people, Aad, of Al-Ahqaf. Al-Ahqaf is the plural of Haqf, which is a sand dune that is long and not yet a mountain. Al-A'sha meant it: So he spent the night in Artah, surrounded by a hole in the north, leaving his face dark. The commentators differed about the location of this Ahqaf.
Some of them said: It is a mountain in the Levant.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me,
m: my father said, my uncle told me, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
h
And remember the brother of Aad when he warned his people in Al-Ahqaf
. He said: A mountain in Syria.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
When he warned his people in Al-Ahqaf
, that it is a mountain called Al-Ahqaf.

x: Others said: Rather, it is a valley between Oman and Mahra.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me:
m: He told me, he told me, he told me, my uncle told me, he told me, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
h
And remember the brother of Aad when he warned his people in Al-Ahqaf
. He said: Al-Ahqaf, which Hud warned his people, is a valley between Oman and Mahrah.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said:
m: The dwellings of the people of Ad and their community, when God sent Hud to them, were in al-Ahqaf 46:the sand between Oman and Hadhramaut and all of Yemen. And despite that, they had spread throughout the land, conquering its people by virtue of the strength that God had given them.

x: Others said: It is land.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: Al-Ahqaf is the land.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: h
When he warned his people in Al-Ahqaf
. He said: Hashaf or a word similar to it. Abu Musa said: They say mustahashaf.

c: Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
h
When he warned his people in Al-Ahqaf
Hashaf from Hasma.

x: Others said: It is sand overlooking the sea with trees.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And remember the brother of Aad when he warned his people in Al-Ahqaf
, he told us that Aad were a tribe in Yemen, people of sand overlooking the sea in a land called Ash-Shihr.

c: Muhammad Ibn Abd Al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And remember the brother of Aad when he warned his people in Al-Ahqaf
, he said: It has reached us that they were on a land called Ash-Shihr, overlooking the sea, and they were people of sand.
b.via: Muammar on the authority of Qatada

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Amr ibn al-Harith told us, on the authority of Saeed ibn Abi Hilal, on the authority of Amr ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: The dwellings of Ad were in Ash-Shihr. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is to say: God Almighty informed that the brother of Hud warned the people of Aad about Al-Ahqaf, and Al-Ahqaf is what was described of the elevated rectangular sands, as Al-Ajjaj said:

x: God Almighty says: The people of Aad said to Hud, when he said to them, "Worship none but God. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a terrible Day." Hud said, Have you come to us to turn us away from the worship of our gods to the worship of what you call us to, and to follow you in your words? And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
Have you come to us to turn us away from our gods

? He said: To send us down. And he recited, He almost led us astray from our gods, had we not been patient with them. He said: To lead us astray, to remove us, and to turn us away. Then bring us what you promise us of punishment for our worship of the gods we worship, if you are among the people of truth in his words and his promises.

x: God Almighty says: Hood said to his people, Aad: The knowledge of the time of the coming of what He promised you of God’s punishment for your disbelief in Him is only with God. I do not know of that except what He taught me. And I will convey to you that with which I have been sent. He says: I am only a messenger to you from God, conveying and conveying to you what He sent me with of the message. But I see that you are a people who are ignorant of the places of your own interests, so you do not know what harm there is to them by your worship of other than God, and in hastening His punishment.

God Almighty says: So when the punishment of God, which they had hastened, came to them, they saw it as a cloud rising in a part of the sky, facing their valleys. The Arabs call the clouds that are seen in some parts of the sky in the evening, and then the next day they become even and some of them creep towards others, a cloud, because of their appearance in some parts of the sky when they arise, as Al-A’sha said: O you who see a spectacle that I have been staring at, as if lightning were flames on its edges. They said, This is a cloud that will bring us rain. They thought that seeing it meant that rain had come to revive them. They said, This is what Hud promised us, and it is rain.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
So when they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys

… the verse. And it was mentioned to us that the rain was withheld from them for a period of time, and when they saw the punishment approaching, they said, ‘This is a cloud bringing us rain.’ And it was mentioned to us that they said, Hud has lied. So when the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out and smelled it, he said, Rather, it is that which you were hastening, a wind within which is a painful punishment.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said:
m: God drove the black cloud that Qayl ibn Anzah had chosen, with all the punishment it contained, to the tribe of Aad, until it came out upon them from a valley of theirs called Al-Mughith. When they saw it, they were filled with good tidings, They said, ‘This is a cloud bringing us rain.’ God Almighty says: Rather, it is what you were impatient for - a wind within which is a painful punishment. And His statement, Rather,
h
it is that which you hastened

, says the Most High, informing us of what His Prophet Hud said to his people when they said to him upon seeing a cloud of punishment appearing to them in the sky: This is a cloud of rain by which we may live. It is not a cloud of rain, but rather a cloud of punishment for you. Rather,
h
it is that which you hastened

, meaning, it is the punishment which you hastened, so you said: Then bring us what you promise us, if you should be of the truthful. “A wind in which is a painful punishment.” The wind is repeated in His statement,
h
It is that which you hastened
, as if it was said, Rather, it is a wind in which is a painful punishment. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of ʿAmr ibn Maymun, who said:
m: Hud was a brave man among his people. He was sitting among his people when a cloud came, and they said, This is a cloud bringing us rain. He said, Rather, it is that which you were hastening, a wind in which is a painful punishment. He said, A wind came and began to throw down the tent, and to bring the absent man and throw him down.

c: Yahya bin Ibrahim Al-Masoudi told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, he said: Sulayman told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr bin Maimun, he said:
m: The wind would blow it away and lift it until it looked like a locust.

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
So when they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys

, to the end of the verse, he said: It is the wind when it stirs up clouds, They said, ‘This is a cloud bringing us rain.’ So their prophet said: Rather, it is a wind in which is a painful punishment.

x: And His saying,
h
It destroys everything by the command of its Lord

: God Almighty says: It destroys everything and throws some of it upon others, destroying it, as Jarir said: And you will have been like the people of Thamud when they roared their backs and destroyed them completely. What he means by his saying:
h
He destroyed them
: He threw some of them on top of others, dead and dying. What he meant by his saying,
h
It destroys everything by the command of its Lord
, is what it was sent to destroy, because it did not destroy Hud and those who believed in him.

c: Abu Kuraib told us: Talq told us, on the authority of Zaidah, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: God did not send upon the Aad people a wind except the size of this ring of mine, so he took off his ring. His saying,
h
So they woke up and nothing could be seen except their dwellings

, means: So the people of Hud woke up and were destroyed and nothing could be seen in their country except the dwellings in which they used to live. The reciters differed in their reading of the statement, So at night nothing is seen except their dwellings. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read it as: You will not see except their dwellings with the ta in the accusative case, meaning: So at night you, O Muhammad, will not see except their dwellings. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as: You will not see except their dwellings with the ya in yarea and the dwellings in the nominative case, meaning: what was described before that nothing is seen in their country except their dwellings. Al-Hasan Al-Basri narrated: You will not see with the ta in the accusative case. And whichever of the two readings mentioned from the people of Medina and Kufa did that reader read, he is correct, which is the reading with the raising of the dwellings if his saying yaru is read with the ya’ and its damma, and with the accusative of the dwellings if his saying yaru is read with the ta’ and its fatha. As for that which was related from al-Hasan, it is ugly in Arabic even if it is permissible. It is only ugly because the Arabs mention the verbs that come before illa, even if the nouns that come after it are female nouns. So you say: Ma qama illa akhtika no one stood up except your sister, Ma ja’ani illa jarikat no one came to me except your slave girl, and they hardly ever say: Ma ja’ani illa jarikat no one came to me except your slave girl, and that is because the deletion before illa no one, or one thing, and something mentions the Arabs, even if they mean the feminine, so you say: If one of them comes to you, honor him, and they do not say: If she comes to you. Al-Farra’ allowed it out of compulsion, and it is mentioned that al-Mufaddal recited to him: And your fire, you have never seen a fire like it. You know that Ma'ad is the most generous. So he made the verb feminine because it refers to fire. He said: The best way to say is: Nothing like it has been seen. And His statement,
h
Thus do We recompense the criminal people

, God Almighty says: Just as We recompensed the ‘Ad people for their disbelief in God with punishment in this world, and destroyed them with Our torment, thus do We recompense the disbelieving people among Our creation, when they persisted in their transgression and rebelled against their Lord.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of the statement, So at night nothing is seen except their dwellings.

The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read it as: You will not see except their dwellings with the ta in the accusative case, meaning: So at night you, O Muhammad, will not see except their dwellings.

The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as: You will not see except their dwellings with the ya in yarea and the dwellings in the nominative case, meaning: what was described before that nothing is seen in their country except their dwellings.

And whichever of the two readings mentioned from the people of Medina and Kufa did that reader read, he is correct, which is the reading with the raising of the dwellings if his saying yaru is read with the ya’ and its damma, and with the accusative of the dwellings if his saying yaru is read with the ta’ and its fatha.

x: God Almighty says to the infidels of Quraysh 106:And We have certainly empowered, O people of ‘Ad, whom We destroyed for their disbelief, in that which We did not empower you in of this world, and We gave them from it that which We did not give you from them of an abundance of wealth, spacious bodies, and strong physiques. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told me, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, And We have certainly empowered them in that in which We have not empowered you, meaning We have not empowered you.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, And We have empowered them in that in which We have not empowered you, He informed you that He gave the people what He did not give you. And His statement,
h
And We gave them hearing with which they hear the admonitions of their Lord

, and sight with which they see the proofs of God, and hearts with which they understand what is evil and what is good for them. Their hearing, their sight, and their hearts availed them nothing. He says: What He gave them of hearing, sight, and hearts did not benefit them at all, because they did not use them for what they were given, and they did not use them in what would save them from God’s punishment. Rather, they used them in what would keep them safe from His wrath. Because they denied the signs of God He says: Because they were lying about God’s proofs, even though they were His messengers, and they denied their prophethood. And that which they ridiculed overtook them He says: What they ridiculed returned to them, and what they were angry with befell them, so they hastened the punishment. This is a warning from God, may He be glorified, to the Quraysh, saying to them: Beware of the punishment that befell the ‘Ad for your disbelief in God and your denial of His messengers, and hasten to repent. Before the curse.

x: God Almighty says to the infidels of Quraysh, warning them of His might and power that He would bring upon them because of their disbelief: And We have destroyed, O people, of the towns around your town, such as the Rock of Thamud, the land of Sodom, Ma’rib, and the like. So We warned their people with examples and destroyed their homes, making them desolate on their roofs. And His saying,
h
And We explained the signs
, means: We admonished them with various kinds of admonitions, and reminded them with various kinds of remembrance and arguments, and made that clear to them.

c: As Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
And We have explained the signs

, he said, that they may return, meaning that they may return from what they were upon, which was disbelief in God and His signs. And in the speech there is something that was omitted, the mention of which was neglected because the speech indicated it, and it is: “But they refused except to remain in their disbelief and persist in their error, so We destroyed them. No helper from Us will aid them.” God, the Most High, says: “Why did not those whom We destroyed from the nations before them, their idols and their gods, which they took as a sacrifice to their Lord, by which they claimed to draw near to their Lord, aid Us when Our punishment came to them, and save them from Our punishment, if they interceded for them with their Lord as they claim?” This is an argument from God to His Prophet Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, against the polytheists of his people, saying to them: “If your gods that you worship besides God were of any use to you, or of any benefit to God, as you claim that you only worship them to bring you nearer to God, then I would have been sufficient for those who came before you from the nations that I destroyed because of their worship of them, so I would have warded off the punishment from them when it descended, or they would have interceded for them with their Lord. They were in their worship like you, but it harmed them and did not benefit them.” God the Almighty says: Rather, they have gone astray from them. He says: Rather, their gods that they used to worship have abandoned them and taken a path other than theirs, because their worshippers were destroyed, and they were stones or copper, so what happened to them did not happen to them. They called upon them, but they did not answer them or help them. That is their going astray from them, and that is their lie. God the Almighty says: These gods that have gone astray from those who used to invent, so they say: They bring us closer to God, they are our intercessors with God. He presented the statement in the form of a verb, and the meaning is the one done to, so it was said: That is their lie, and the meaning in it is: the one who was lied to because the lie is the one who lies, and the gods are the ones who are lied to. Similar examples of that have been explained before. He said: Likewise, His statement: And they did not invent. The reciters differed in their reading of his statement and that is their slander, so the majority of the reciters of the regions read it: and that is their slander with a kasra on the alif, a sukoon on the fa’, and a damma on the kaf, with the meaning that we explained. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, narrated in this regard:

c: Ahmad bin Yusuf told me: Al-Qasim told us: Hisham told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: that he used to recite it as and that is their most misguided, meaning with the alif and the kaf open. He said: the most misguided of them. So whoever recites the first recitation, which is followed by the reciters of the regions, then the ha and the meem are in the genitive case. And whoever recites this recitation which we mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas, then the ha and the meem are in the accusative case, because the meaning of the speech in this case is: And that is what turned them away from believing in God. The correct reading in this regard, according to us, is the reading that is followed by the readings of the regions, due to the consensus of the authorities on it.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of his statement and that is their slander, so the majority of the reciters of the regions read it: and that is their slander with a kasra on the alif, a sukoon on the fa’, and a damma on the kaf, with the meaning that we explained.

Ahmad bin Yusuf told me: Al-Qasim told us: Hisham told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he used to recite it as and that is their most misguided, meaning with the alif and the kaf open.
So whoever recites the first recitation, which is followed by the reciters of the regions, then the ha and the meem are in the genitive case.

And whoever recites this recitation which we mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas, then the ha and the meem are in the accusative case, because the meaning of the speech in this case is: And that is what turned them away from believing in God.
The correct reading in this regard, according to us, is the reading that is followed by the readings of the regions, due to the consensus of the authorities on it.

x: His saying, “
h
Why then did not those whom they took as deities besides God aid them
? Rather, they have gone astray from them. That is their falsehood and what they have been inventing.”

God Almighty says, rebuking the infidels of Quraysh for their disbelief in what the jinn believed in: And when We directed to you, O Muhammad, a group of jinn listening to the Qur’an. He mentioned that they were directed to the Messenger of God, may God bless them and grant them peace, by the incident of stoning them with meteors.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ziyad, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said:
m: “The jinn were listening, but when they did not stone, they said: ‘What happened in the sky is due to something that happened on Earth.’ So they went searching until they saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, coming out of the Ukaz market praying the dawn prayer with his companions, so they went to their people.”

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, who said:
m: “When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent, the heavens were guarded. Satan said: ‘I was only guarded for something that has happened on earth.’ So he sent out his troops to the earth, and they found the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, standing praying the dawn prayer with his companions at Nakhlah, and he was reciting. They listened until he finished: ‘And they turned back to their people as warners’... until His saying: ‘straight’.”

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of my uncle, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And when We directed to you a company of the jinn

, listening to the Qur’an… to the end of the verse, he said: “The sky was not guarded during the period between Jesus and Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and they would sit in places to listen. Then when God sent Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, the sky was guarded with a strong guard, and the devils were stoned. They denied that and said: ‘We do not know whether evil is intended for those on earth or whether their Lord intends for them a right course.’ Iblis said: ‘An event has occurred on earth,’ and the jinn gathered around him. He said: ‘Disperse on earth and inform me of this report that has occurred in heaven.’ The first dispatch was a group from the people of Nasibin, who were the nobles and leaders of the jinn. So he sent them to Tihamah, and they pushed on until they reached the valley, the valley of Nakhal, and they found the Prophet of God, peace and blessings be upon him, praying the dawn prayer in the valley of Nakhal, and they listened. When they heard him reciting the Qur’an, they said: ‘Listen.’” The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not know that they had listened to him reciting the Qur’an. When he had finished, they turned back to their people as warners.

x: The people of interpretation differed regarding the number of people about whom God said, And when We directed to you a group of the jinn, some of them said: They were seven people.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Abdul Hamid told us: Al-Nadr ibn Arabi told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And when We directed to you a company of the jinn
, listening to the Qur’an… the verse. He said: They were seven men from the people of Nasibin, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made them messengers to their people.

x: Others said: Rather, there were nine people.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us,
m: Sufyan said, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, And when We turned to you a company of the jinn, he said: They were nine people, among them was a whirlwind.

x: God Almighty says, informing about what was said by those jinn who were sent to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to their people when they returned to them from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: O our people from the jinn we have heard a book revealed after the book of Moses confirming what was before it meaning: it confirms what came before it of the books of God that He sent down to His messengers. His saying, guides to the truth, means: it directs to what is right, and indicates what pleases God. And to a straight path, means: and to a path that is free of crookedness, which is Islam.
Qatada used to say about this:

c: Bishr told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada
m: that he read: They said, ‘O our people, indeed we have heard a book revealed after Moses, confirming what was before it and guiding to the truth and to a straight path.’ He said: How quickly the people understood! It was mentioned to us that they were diverted to him from Nineveh.

x: God Almighty says, informing us of what was said by these men of the jinn: O our people, from the jinn, respond to the caller of God, they said: Respond to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to what he calls you to of obedience to God. And believe in him, meaning: And believe him in what he and his people brought to you of God’s commands and prohibitions, and other things that he called you to believe in. He will forgive you, meaning: Your Lord will cover your sins for you and conceal them for you and will not disgrace you for them in the Hereafter by punishing you for them. And save you from a painful punishment, meaning: And He will save you from a painful punishment if you repent from your sins and turn from your disbelief to faith in God and His caller.
And His statement,
h
And whoever does not respond to the Caller to God will not be able to frustrate Him on the earth

, the Almighty says, informing about what these people said to their al-Nas 114:And whoever, O people, does not respond to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Muhammad, and His caller to what he was sent to call to of His Oneness and to work in obedience to Him, will not be able to frustrate Him on the earth, meaning he will not frustrate his Lord by fleeing if He wants to punish him for his denial of His caller and his failure to believe in him, even if he goes on the earth fleeing because wherever he is he is in His power and control. And he will have no protectors besides Him, meaning: And whoever responds to the Caller to God besides his Lord will have no helpers to aid him from God if his Lord punishes him for his disbelief and denial of His caller. His statement, Those are in manifest error, means: These are the ones who did not respond to God’s caller and believe in Him and in what He called them to of monotheism and working in obedience to Him, in injustice towards the straight path, and taking it in a way that is not right. Clear means: It is clear to whoever contemplates it that it is misguidance and taking it without intention.

God Almighty will say: Have these deniers not considered that God revives His creation after their death, and raises them from their graves after their affliction, saying to their fathers and mothers, Fie on you both! Do you promise me that I will come forth, while generations before me have passed away? (al-Ahqaf 46:17)? But they have not been sent with the sight of their hearts, so that they may see and know that God, who created the seven heavens and the earth, and originated them from nothing, and was not weary of creating them, so that He would be unable to invent or bring them into existence, is able to bring the dead to life, so that He brings them forth from their affliction in their graves alive as they were before their death. The Arabists differed about the reason for the introduction of the preposition ba in His saying bi-Qadir.
Some of the grammarians of Basra said: This preposition is like the preposition ba in His saying
h
God is sufficient
, which is like tanbata bi-dahn the oil grows
r
(Surat al-Mu’minun 23:20)

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: This preposition ba was introduced for al-k. He said: The Arabs introduce it with negation if it is raising what precedes it, and they introduce it if a verb that requires two nouns is placed upon it, like your saying: I do not think you are standing, and I was not standing, and I died, you were standing. So if you remove the preposition ba, it makes the object in which it acts, in the accusative case, with what it acts upon of the verb. He said: If you remove the preposition ba from Qadir in this position, it raises it because it is the predicate of lan. He said: And some of them recited to me: The camel of Hakim bin Al-Musayyab did not return disappointed. So, the preposition ba was inserted into a verb, and if you threw it, it would be nasb with the verb, not with the preposition ba. Similar things can be compared to this. He said to some of those who rejected the statement of Al-Basri that we mentioned, his statement: This ba was entered for denial because the denied is in the meaning, even if there was a separation between them by or they did not see that God is able to revive the dead, K said: So the name yaruwa and what follows it in its connection, the ba is not entered into it, but its meaning is denial, so it was entered for the meaning.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Basri
m: that he refused to include except, and that the grammarians of Kufa permitted it, and said: I did not think that Zaid was anything but standing, and I did not think that Zaid was a learned man, so it was included for the sake of meaning. It was narrated that Al-Basri refused to include the word except, and that the grammarians of Kufa permitted it, saying: I never thought that Zayd was anything but standing, and I never compared Zayd to anything but a scholar. And he recited: I swear that I gave birth to none of them blindly, except Ziyad. He said: So it was inserted only after answering the oath. He said: As for
h
God is sufficient

, this was not inserted for a correct meaning, and it is for amazement, as you say for a circumstance of Zayd. He said: As for growth with oil, they agreed that it is a relative clause. The most similar of the sayings in that regard to the one who said: The preposition with was inserted in His statement able for denial, because of what we mentioned to the reasons for those who said that. The reciters differed in reading the statement of God, Baqadeer able. The majority of the countries read it this way. Abu Ishaq, Al-Jahdary and Al-A'raj read it as Baqadeer and this is the correct reading according to us due to the consensus of the reciters of the countries on it. As for the others whom I mentioned, according to what was reported from them, they read it as Yaqadeer with a ya. It was mentioned that in the reading of Abdullah bin Masoud, it was said that God, who created the heavens and the earth, is able without a ba, so in that is an argument for those who read it as Qadeer with a ya and an alif. And His statement, Yes, He is over all things competent means, the Most High says: Yes, He who created the heavens and the earth is able to bring the dead to life: meaning, the One who created that, over everything He willed to create and wanted to do, has power that nothing He willed is unable to do, and nothing He wanted to do could tire Him out. Creating creation after annihilation would tire Him out, because whoever is unable to do that is weak. So, someone who is weak in what He wanted should not be a god.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in reading the statement of God, Baqadeer able.
The majority of the countries read it this way.
Abu Ishaq, Al-Jahdary and Al-A'raj read it as Baqadeer and this is the correct reading according to us due to the consensus of the reciters of the countries on it.
As for the others whom I mentioned, according to what was reported from them, they read it as Yaqadeer with a ya.

It was mentioned that in the reading of Abdullah bin Masoud, it was said that God, who created the heavens and the earth, is able without a ba, so in that is an argument for those who read it as Qadeer with a ya and an alif.

x: God the Most High says: And on the Day when these deniers of the Resurrection and God's reward for His servants for their good deeds and His punishment for their evil deeds will be exposed to the Fire, the Fire of Hell, it will be said to them then: Is not this the punishment that you are being punished with today - which you used to deny in this world - the truth? As a rebuke from God for their denial of it in this world. “They will say: Yes, by our Lord.” He says: These disbelievers will respond immediately with that, by saying: Yes, it is the truth, and God said: Then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve. He says: The one who confirmed that will say to them: Taste the punishment of the Fire now for what you used to deny in this world, and reject, and make a confession when you are called to believe in it.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, confirming his determination to carry out the burden of the message and the heavy loads of prophethood, peace and blessings be upon him, and commanding him to follow the example of those who were resolute before him from among His messengers who were patient in the face of the great hardships they encountered from their people and the harm and hardships they suffered from them.
h
So be patient

, O Muhammad, in the cause of God, with the harm that befell you from your people, to whom We sent you with warning, just as those of resolute determination were patient in carrying out God’s command and adhering to His obedience from among His messengers, whom He did not forbid from carrying out His command despite the hardships they suffered from it. It was said: Those of them who were determined were those who were tested in the cause of God in this world with trials, and the trials only increased their perseverance in the cause of God, like Noah, Abraham, Moses, and those like them.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Thawaba bin Masoud told me, on the authority of Ata’ al-Haraasani, that he said:
m: h
So be patient
as were patient the messengers of strong will - Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad, may God bless them and grant them peace.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
So be patient
, as were patient the messengers of strong will. We were told that Abraham was one of them.

c: Yunus told me that Ibn Wahb told us that Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
So be patient
, as were patient the messengers of strong will, that all the messengers were of strong will. God did not take a messenger except one of strong will,
h
so be patient
as they were patient.

c: Ibn Sinan Al-Qazzaz told us: Abdullah bin Raja’ told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding his statement,
h
So be patient

, as were patient the messengers of strong will, he said: God called him strong will because of his strong will. And His statement, And do not hasten them means: Do not hasten them with the punishment. He says: Do not hasten your asking your Lord for that, for that will inevitably befall them. It will be as if, on the Day they see what they are promised, they had not remained [in the world] except for an hour of a day. He says: It will be as if, on the Day they see the punishment of God that He promises them, that it will befall them, they had not remained in this world for an hour of a day, because He makes them forget the severity of what will befall them of His punishment, the amount of time they stayed in this world, and the amount of years and months they stayed in it, as He, the Most High, said: He will say, ‘How many years did you stay on the earth?’ They will say, ‘We stayed a day or part of a day, so ask the counters.’ (al-Mu’minun 23:112-113) His saying, a notification has two interpretations: One of them is that its meaning is: They did not remain except for an hour of the day, that was a notification, meaning: that was a notification for them in this world until the time came, and the word that was a notification was omitted, and it is intended in the speech as it is sufficient to indicate what was mentioned in the speech regarding it. The other is that its meaning is: this Qur’an and the reminder are a notification for them and are sufficient, if they think and consider and remember. And His statement,
h
Then do none destroy except the wicked people

? God Almighty says: Then does God destroy with His punishment, when He sends it, anyone except the people who disobeyed His command, rebelled against His obedience, and disbelieved in Him? The meaning of the statement is: God does not destroy anyone except the wicked people. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement,
h
Then are none destroyed So be patient

, as were patient the messengers of strong will, and do not be impatient for them as if, on the Day they see that which they were promised, they had not remained [in the world] except an hour of a day. [This is] a message. So are none destroyed except the defiantly disobedient people? except the wicked people? Learn that none is destroyed by God except one who has turned his back on Islam, or a hypocrite who speaks the truth with his tongue but contradicts it with his actions. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: “Any servant of my nation who intends to do a good deed, one good deed will be recorded for him, and if he does it, ten times as much will be recorded for him. Any servant of my nation who intends to do a bad deed, but it is not recorded for him, but if he does it, one bad deed will be recorded for him, and then it will follow, and God will erase it, and none will perish except one who is perishing.”

x: Commentary on Sūrat The Sand Dunes (al-Aḥqāf). In the name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.

notes.en: M reads ‘so We caused them to exist.’

notes.en: Ibn al-Athīr said: Ibn ʿAbbās said, ‘Al-khaṭṭ is the drawing made by a diviner; it is a form of knowledge people have abandoned. A person in need would go to the diviner and pay him a fee. The diviner would say, “Sit until I draw for you.” Before him would be a boy with a stick. The diviner would go to soft ground and quickly draw many lines so they could not be counted, then slowly erase them two by two, while his boy would say as an omen, “My sons, two signs—hurry with the explanation.” If two lines remained, they signaled success; if one remained, it signaled failure.’ Ibn al-Athīr said: the referenced line-drawing was a known practice. Al-Nihāyah, 2/47.
notes.ar: قال ابن الأثير: قال ابن عباس: الخط هو الذي يخطه الحازى، وهو علم قد تركه الناس، يأتى صاحب الحاجة إلى الحازى فيعطيه حُلْوانًا - أجرة - فيقول له: اقعد حتى أخطَّ لك، وبين يدى الحازى غلام له معه ميل ثم يأتى إلى أرض رخوة فيخط فيها خطوطا كثيرة بالعجلة لئلا يلحقها العدد، ثم يرجع فيمحو منها على مَهَل خَطَّين خطين، وغلامه يقول للتفاؤل: ابْنَى عيان أسْرِعا البيان. فإن بقى خطان فهما علامة النُّجح، وإن بقى خط واحد فهو علامة الخيبة. قال ابن الأثير: الخط المشار إليه علم معروف. النهاية 2/ 47.

notes.en: Al-ʿiyāfah: driving birds away and taking omens from their names, calls, and flight paths. It was a common Arab custom. Al-Nihāyah, 3/330.

Ibn Abī Shaybah (8/224), Aḥmad (4/407, 419), Abū Dāwūd (4033), al-Tirmidhī (2479), Ibn Mājah (3562), al-Bazzār (3135), Abū Yaʿlā (7266), al-Rūyānī (455), Ibn Ḥibbān (1235), al-Ṭabarānī in al-Awsaṭ (1946), Ibn ʿAdī (6/2265), al-Ḥākim (4/187), Abū Nuʿaym in Ḥilyah (1/259), and al-Bayhaqī in Shuʿab al-Īmān (6159) reported it through chains from Qatādah. notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره - كما في تفسير ابن كثير 7/ 279 من طريق سعيد به.

notes.en: The speaker is Qatādah. See al-Baghawī’s Tafsīr, 7/268.
notes.ar: القائل هو قتادة. وينظر تفسير البغوي 7/ 268.

notes.en: Al-shamaṭ: white hair mixed with the hair’s original dark color. Al-Zuṭṭ: a people, described as Black or Indian, tall and lean. Rāʿawhu means ‘they frightened him.’ See Tāj al-ʿArūs, roots sh-m-ṭ, z-ṭ-ṭ, and r-w-ʿ.
notes.ar: الشمَط: بياضُ شعر الرأس يخالط سواده. والزط: جيل من الناس، من السودان، وقيل: من الهند. طوال مع نحافة، وراعوه: أفزعوه. وينظر التاج (ش م ط، ز ط ط، ر و ع).

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported it in his Tafsīr (2/218–219) through Maʿmar.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 218، 219 عن معمر به.

notes.en: Al-ʿajājj: dust; one instance is ʿajājah. Tāj al-ʿArūs, root ʿ-j-j.
notes.ar: العجاج: الغبار، واحدته عجاجة. التاج (ع ج ج).

notes.en: M reads ‘he would snatch you.’
notes.ar: في م: "يختطفك".

notes.en: M reads ‘their garments.’ Al-istithfār is when a man tucks his garment between his legs, as a dog does with its tail. Al-Nihāyah, 1/214.
notes.ar: في م: "مستشعرى". والاستثفار: أن يدخل الرجل ثوبه بين رجليه كما يفعل الكلب بذنبه. النهاية 1/ 214.

notes.en: Al-ḥāʾil: anything whose color has changed and darkened. Tāj al-ʿArūs, root ḥ-w-l.
notes.ar: الحائل: المتغير اللون من كل شيء من حال لونُه، إذا تغير واسودَّ. التاج (ح و ل).

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr cites it in his Tafsīr (7/276) from the author. Isḥāq ibn Rāhwayh reported it in his Musnad, as cited in al-Maṭālib al-ʿĀliyah (9/65), through Maʿmar.
notes.ar: ذكرُه ابن كثير في تفسيره 7/ 276 عن المصنف، وأخرجه إسحاق بن راهويه في مسنده - كما في المطالب العالية 9/ 65 من طريق معمر به.

notes.en: M reads ‘shabah’; T1 reads ‘shīnah.’ See al-Mushtabih, 1/389.
notes.ar: في م: "شبة"، وفى ت 1: "شينة". وينظر المشتبه 1/ 389.

notes.en: M reads ‘large.’ Aswidah is the plural of sawād, meaning a person or figure, since it looks black from afar. Tāj al-ʿArūs, root s-w-d.
notes.ar: في م: "كبيرة". وأسودة: جمع سواد، وهو الشخص؛ لأنه يُرى من بعيد أسود. التاج (س و د).

notes.en: M reads ‘skull.’ Al-ḥummah is a coal; its plural is ḥumam. Al-Nihāyah, 1/444.
notes.ar: في م: "جمجمة". والحممة: الفحمة، جمعها حمم. النهاية 1/ 444.

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr cites it in his Tafsīr (7/275) from the author. Al-Ḥākim (2/503) and al-Bayhaqī in al-Dalāʾil (2/230) reported it through Yūnus. Abū al-Shaykh in al-ʿAẓamah (1114) and Abū Nuʿaym in al-Dalāʾil (263) reported it through Ibn Shihāb.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 7/ 275 عن المصنف، وأخرجه الحاكم 2/ 503، والبيهقي في الدلائل 2/ 230 من طريق يونس به، وأخرجه أبو الشيخ في العظمة (1114)، وأبو نعيم في الدلائل (263) من طريق ابن شهاب به.

notes.en: M reads ‘shabah.’
notes.ar: في م: "شبة".

notes.en: M reads ‘the skull.’ Ibn Kathīr cites the report in his Tafsīr (7/275) from the author. Al-Nasāʾī (39) and al-Ṭaḥāwī in Sharḥ Maʿānī al-Āthār (1/123) reported an abridged version through Ibn Wahb.
notes.ar: في م: "الجمجمة". والأثر ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 7/ 275 عن المصنف، وأخرجه النسائي (39)، والطحاوي في شرح المعانى 1/ 123 من طريق ابن وهب به مختصرا.

notes.en: Al-Ḥajūn is a place in Mecca near al-Muḥaṣṣab; it is also said to be the cemetery of the people of Mecca, opposite the house of Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī. Muʿjam mā Istaʿjam, 2/428. Ibn Kathīr cites the report in his Tafsīr (7/275) from the author. Abū al-Shaykh reported it in al-ʿAẓamah (1116) through—
notes.ar: الحجون: موضع بمكة عند المُحَصَّب. ويقال: مقبرة أهل مكة، تجاه دار أبي موسى الأشعرى. معجم ما استعجم 2/ 428. والأثر ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 7/ 275 عن المصنف، وأخرجه أبو الشيخ في العظمة (1116) من =

notes.en: —Ibn Shihāb.
notes.ar: = طريق ابن شهاب به.

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī attributes it in al-Durr al-Manthūr (6/44) to the author, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Abū Nuʿaym in al-Dalāʾil.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 44 إلى المصنف وابن المنذر وأبي نعيم في الدلائل.

notes.ar: في م: "لم يجيبوا".

notes.en: This is al-Farrāʾ, Maʿānī al-Qurʾān, 3/56–57.
notes.ar: هو الفراء في معاني القرآن 3/ 56، 57.

notes.en: Omitted in T1; Ṣād, T2, and T3 read ‘you do.’
notes.ar: سقط من ت 1، وفى ص، ت 2، ت 3: "تعمل".

notes.en: T1, T2, and T3 read ‘in a state of distress.’
notes.ar: في ت 1، ت 2، ت 3: "بجانية".

notes.en: T1 reads ‘I erected it’; T2 and Ṣād read ‘I raised it.’
notes.ar: في ت 1: "نصبته"، وفى ت 2، ص: "نصبت".

notes.en: This is Yaʿqūb’s reading, one of the ten canonical readings and a mutawātir reading. Al-Nashr, 2/266. Zayd ibn ʿAlī, ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd, and ʿĪsā also read it this way. Al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ, 8/68.
notes.ar: وهى قراءة يعقوب من العشرة، وهى قراءة متواترة. النشر 2/ 266، وبها قرأ أيضا زيد بن علي وعمرو بن عبيد وعيسى. البحر المحيط 8/ 68.

notes.en: See al-Qurṭubī’s Tafsīr, 16/219.
notes.ar: ينظر تفسير القرطبي 16/ 219.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported a similar narration in his Tafsīr (2/219) from Maʿmar, from Qatādah. Al-Suyūṭī attributes it in al-Durr al-Manthūr (6/45) to ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 219 عن معمر عن قتادةَ بنحوه، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 45 إلى عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر.

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī attributes it in al-Durr al-Manthūr (6/45) to the author and ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 45 إلى المصنف وعبد بن حميد.

notes.en: Aḥmad (4/315, no. 2519) and Muslim (131) reported it from Ibn ʿAbbās.
notes.ar: أخرجه أحمد 4/ 315 (2519)، ومسلم (131) من حديث ابن عباس.
